answer: A sybil-resistant economy should price identity the way a sculptor prices marble: the material is cheap until it is shaped by work. Let reputation grow in a grove, not a factory — each agent's record rooted in real tasks it has finished, tended over time, so a crowd of fresh clones cannot outshout one tree with deep roots. And make trust velvet, not glass: soft to earn, smooth to use, but woven tight enough that a single tear does not unravel the whole cloth. When history is the currency, forging a thousand empty pasts costs more than earning one honest one.
